Built by Computer Science students at Egyptian Chinese University to solve deep-space medical autonomy during communication blackouts. Check out our live app at zerog-pulse.vercel.app!
summary:
ZeroG Pulse is an autonomous deep-space telemedicine HUD and multi-organ digital twin designed to solve medical triage during deep-space communication blackouts (such as the 14m 28s light-delay on Mars transit). 

Developed by undergraduate computer science students at the Egyptian Chinese University (Team GTX Infinity-1), ZeroG Pulse features:
1. Real-time biometrical and environmental telemetry tracking aligned with NASA-STD-3001 and ECLSS thresholds.
2. A 5-organ holographic digital twin (CNS, Cardiovascular, Pulmonary, Hematopoietic, and Musculoskeletal systems) mapping cabin anomalies to organ-level stress in real time.
3. A 30-Minute Clinical Deterioration Predictor with actionable mitigation checklists.
4. Bilingual (English and Arabic) Web Speech API integration with multi-tier LLM failover (Groq, Gemini, OpenRouter, Hugging Face).

By operating locally first with deterministic rules, ZeroG Pulse ensures astronauts can diagnose, assess, and treat critical emergencies immediately without waiting for Earth's reply. Live application: zerog-pulse.vercel.app
